name: Kevin John Duska
note: Born in Montréal by his son's statement (S-000-5). That puts his father, Ahn 4, in Montréal by 1962. A Québec statistical return of marriage of 1984 names his father as Steve Duska, born in Czechoslovakia, who also signs as a witness (S-249; image held). The link to Ahn 4 no longer rests on a statement alone. The bride of 1984 was Lyne Lefebvre, born in Montréal in 1964, Kevin's mother, who has died by his statement (S-000-10). She is named here as his wife; her own line is outside this rebuild. Named as the grandson Kevin in Mike Duska's death notice of 1974 (D-006-20).
living_basis: Kevin does not know whether his father is living (ledger v8, X-016). Shown by name and year only.

name: Štefan (Stefan, Steve) Duska
note: Son of Michal Duska, Roman Catholic cottar of Senné, and Maria Demko, Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce, by a sealed parish certificate of 1947. Born in Slovakia, not in Canada. Known as Steve; died 2018 (stated, no record in hand). He left Iňačovce with his mother in November 1937, aged 8, on her passport, and sailed from Antwerp for Montréal to join his father (S-252 to S-254). Three papers of 1937 give his birthday as 23 October 1929; the parish certificate has 21 October, which is kept here as the church's own entry. In 1984 he is 'Steve Duska, born in Czechoslovakia' (S-249). Married Joan Teresa Leonard at St. Dominic's Church, Montréal, on 26 November 1955; then a superintendent, living at 5218A Des Érables (D-006-22, image held). A second parish extract of his baptism was issued at Senné on 1 October 1955 (D-006-21).
living_basis: Died in 2018 by Kevin's statement to the coordinator (S-000-6).

baptism.place: Roman Catholic parish church, Senné (register vol. IV, p. 110, entry 43)

name: Joan Teresa Leonard
note: Wife of Stephen (Štefan) Duska by the registration of their marriage, Montréal, 26 November 1955. Entered by name only; her own line is outside this rebuild (ruling X-022) and nothing else from the record is used.
living_basis: No death on record here; shown by name only.

name: Michal (Mihály, Mike) Duska
note: Born 3 July 1903 at Senné, house 79, son of András Duska, cottar, and Anna Nyemcsik (baptism D-009-79). Identified by the census of 1930: his wife Maria and son Štefan are entered at Senné 145 as the daughter-in-law and grandson of Andrej Duška and Anna, married 18 January 1892 (D-011-24). Married Maria Demko on 30 January 1927 by that census. Roman Catholic cottar of Senné 160 in 1929. Sailed for Canada aged 26, with Mikulas Duska, between November 1929 and July 1930 (D-006-19); naturalised 22 April 1940; at 1196a St. George Street, Montréal, in 1937, when he sent for his family; 'Mike Duska' on his wife's stone; alive in November 1966. Died at the Montreal General Hospital on 31 January 1974, 'age 71'; funeral from the Slovak church of St. Cyril and Method; buried in Côte-des-Neiges cemetery (D-006-20). The notice names two sons, Steve and Mike.

name: Maria Demko (Mary Demko)
note: Wife of Michal Duska and mother of Štefan by the 1947 certificate; Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce. Died at Montréal on 9 September 1950 by her husband's declaration of 1966. Stone: born 1906, died 1950. Her parents are the Demko agent's to establish: it has Mihály Demkó and Mária Kocsis (DM P-018, P-019 @57861ad). Her emigrant passport of 1937 gives her birth as 22 August 1906 at Iňačovce and her occupation as farmer; she left in November 1937 with her son. The census of 1930 has her at Senné 145 in her father-in-law's house, married 30 January 1927, with a birth date of 15 August 1907 that disagrees with her passport. Her state birth registration, no. 45 of 1906 at Alsókánya, is read here too (D-X01-04): daughter of Mihály Demkó, born at Magasrév, aged 24, and Mária Kocsis, born at Solymos, aged 20.

name: András (Andrej) Duska
note: Roman Catholic servant, then cottar and day-labourer of Senné: houses 73, 92, 79, 98, 138 and, in 1930, 145. Married Anna Nyemcsik on 18 January 1892. Father of Michal by the census of 1930 and the baptism of 1903. Could not read or write. Son of György Duska and Anna Krak by his marriage entry (D-006-03). A death date of 22 August 1940 is noted beside a baptism of [1868] with those parents (D-009-06); the day of that baptism is not on the strip. At his marriage in 1892 he was living at Hrabó, a farmstead of Senné.

name: Anna Nyemcsik (Nemčíková; written Minarcsin and Nyemecz)
note: Wife of András Duska from 18 January 1892; twelve children, nine living in 1930. Her birth date in the census is the date of the baptism of Anna, daughter of János Nyemcsik and Erzsébet Hresko, in the Senné register (H-051). She could read.

name: György Duska (the elder)
note: Roman Catholic cottar of Senné, house 6, from [1866]; called 'the elder' from 1875. Named as the father of the groom András Duska in the marriage entry of 18 January 1892. Children by Anna Krak from [1866] to [1875]; a second wife, Mária Kozej, by 1880 (H-052). His own birth and parents are not known; whether he came from Solymos is hypothesis H-057. Greek Catholic Duskas were at Szenna a generation before him: Joannes (d. 1830 aged 61) and a Maria, widow of Georgius (d. 1874 aged 65), who may be his mother (H-079, H-080).

name: Anna Krak
note: Greek Catholic. Named as the mother of the groom in the marriage entry of 1892, with a word after her name read 'I[sk]e' [?], perhaps her village. Mother of György Duska's children from [1866] to [1875]. Two baptisms of an Anna Krak in 1848 are candidates for hers, at Sztára and at Jesztreb (H-055, 20; H-056, 35); neither is attached. One of the two is now out: the Jesztreb Anna died on 8 December [1848] at about eight weeks (D-013-36). Three girls named Anna Krak with a father János died at Jesztreb as children, in [1836], [1847] and [1848].

name: János Nyemcsik
note: Roman Catholic cottar of Senné, house 79 ([1866] to 1872), then 77. Named as the father of the bride in the marriage entry of 1892 and of Anna in her baptism of 24 August 1872. Several men of this name lived at Senné; this one is fixed by his wife.

name: Erzsébet Hresko, alias Minarcsin
note: Named as the mother of the bride in the marriage entry of 1892 and of Anna in 1872. Two baptisms write her 'Hresko alias Minarcsin'; her daughter is entered as Anna Minarcsin at her own children's baptisms in the 1890s.
